translationRepairs: At the opening of Tiancheng (560) he was sent out as bearer of the staff and interior minister of Nankang.
At the opening of Tianjia (560) he was sent out as bearer of the staff and interior minister of Nankang.
天嘉 is the Chen era Tianjia; Tiancheng (天成) is a different reign name. AD 560 matches Tianjia 1, and the rest of the proposed sentence matches 出為持節、南康內史.
At the beginning of Tiancheng he went out as Bearer of the Staff and Interior Minister of Nankang.
At the beginning of Tianjia he went out as Bearer of the Staff and Interior Minister of Nankang.
天嘉 romanizes as Tianjia, not Tiancheng; the proposed literal correctly replaces only that misreading.
In the Taiping turmoil he received acting credentials as fierce-martial general and army commander.
In the Taiqing turmoil he received acting credentials as fierce-martial general and army commander.
太清 is Liang Taiqing; Taiping (太平) is a different era. Context with Hou Jing confirms the Taiqing disaster reading.
In the turmoil of Taiping he was given acting staff, made Fierce Martial General, and made army commander.
In the turmoil of Taiqing he was given acting staff, made Fierce Martial General, and made army commander.
太清 must be Taiqing, not Taiping; the proposed literal restores the correct reign name without other changes.

In the first year of Tiancheng (560) he was made bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-the-south general and inspector of Xiang, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang with one thousand households.

In the first year of Tianjia (560) he was made bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-the-south general and inspector of Xiang, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang with one thousand households.
天嘉元年 is Tianjia 1 (AD 560), not Tiancheng; the proposed idiomatic keeps the offices and enfeoffment intact.

In the first year of Tiancheng he was given Bearer of the Staff, Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Pacifying-the-South General, and Inspector of Xiang, enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang county with a fief of one thousand households.

In the first year of Tianjia he was given Bearer of the Staff, Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Pacifying-the-South General, and Inspector of Xiang, enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang county with a fief of one thousand households.
天嘉元年 is Tianjia year 1; replacing Tiancheng with Tianjia corrects the era romanization only.
